title: Data on firm headquarters based on SEC EDGAR filings
text: Data on firm headquarters based on SEC EDGAR filings. Dates related to SEC filing dates. Rather than provide dates for all filings, data are aggregated into groups of filings by state and CIK and dates are collapsed into windows over which all filings for a given CIK were associated with a given state. For example, CIK 0000037755 has filings with a CA headquarters from 1994-06-02 until 1996-03-25, then filings with an OH headquarters from 1996-05-30 until 1999-04-05, then filings with a CA headquarters from 1999-06-11 onwards. To ensure continuous coverage over the sample period, it is assumed that any change in state occurs the day after the last observed filing for the previous state.

title: Data on public float
text:
Details
Five public-float dates have been corrected against the companies’ Form 10-K cover pages: Spectrum Control (CIK 92769), fiscal year 2004, and Whitehall Jewellers (CIK 868984), fiscal years 2003–2006. These corrections replace four fractional values of pfyear and correct four months, with corresponding updates to pfdate. The original source CSV is preserved. The original values, corrected dates, and filing links are recorded in data-raw/iliev_2010_date_corrections.csv in the source repository; see also the investigation and filing evidence (https://github.com/iangow/farr/issues/28). Other source anomalies, including invalid dates represented by missing values, remain in the data.

title: namespaces.EraExpr
text:
Methods



Name
Description




div_if_pos
Divide by other only when the denominator is strictly positive.


ntile
Assign observations to n approximately equal-sized buckets.


truncate
Set values outside type-2 quantile cutoffs to null.


winsorize
Clip values to type-2 quantile cutoffs, following farr::winsorize().




div_if_pos
era_pl.namespaces.EraExpr.div_if_pos(other)
Divide by other only when the denominator is strictly positive.
The result is null when the denominator is zero, negative, or null. This is convenient for ratio construction in accounting-style pipelines where non-positive denominators are usually treated as invalid.


ntile
era_pl.namespaces.EraExpr.ntile(n)
Assign observations to n approximately equal-sized buckets.
This mirrors the common SQL/R ntile idea and is typically used with .over(...) to create within-group deciles, quintiles, and similar ranked portfolios. Null values remain null and are excluded when bucket sizes are calculated.


truncate
era_pl.namespaces.EraExpr.truncate(prob=0.01, p_low=None, p_high=None)
Set values outside type-2 quantile cutoffs to null.
Argument resolution matches :meth:winsorize.


winsorize
era_pl.namespaces.EraExpr.winsorize(prob=0.01, p_low=None, p_high=None)
Clip values to type-2 quantile cutoffs, following farr::winsorize().
Argument handling mirrors the R helper:

winsorize(prob=0.01) is equivalent to winsorize(p_low=0.01, p_high=0.99).
If p_low and/or p_high are supplied, those explicit cutoffs are used in preference to the defaults implied by prob.
If prob=None, only the explicitly supplied side(s) are applied, so one-sided winsorization is possible.

title: Function reference
text:
Polars event dates and Parquet
These helpers work with Polars frames. Functions that read CRSP data require access to those data. get_event_rets() and copy_inline() are not implemented in era_pl; the Ibis event-return API is listed below.



get_trading_dates
Create a trading-date index from a CRSP daily index table.


get_annc_dates
Map all calendar dates onto the next available trading day.


get_event_dates
Expand event dates into trading-day windows.


load_parquet
Scan a parquet table from a WRDS-style local data directory.


cast_decimals
Cast all decimal columns in frame to Float64.

Polars external data

title: NumberedLines
text:
A sequence of text lines that preserves original line numbers.
NumberedLines behaves like a read-only sequence of strings, but carries an explicit index attribute that records the original (global) line numbers for each line. This is useful when working with text extracted from external sources (e.g., PDFs, logs, or scraped documents) where line numbers are meaningful for debugging, citation, or reproducibility.
The object supports slicing and filtering while preserving original line numbers. Slicing returns a new NumberedLines object whose index reflects the corresponding subset of the original indices. The index can be reset explicitly using reset_index().

title: NumberedLines
text:
Parameters









Name
Type
Description
Default




lines
str or Iterable[str]
Either a single string containing newline-separated text, or an iterable of strings. If a string is provided, it is split into lines using str.splitlines(). If an iterable of strings is provided (e.g., page-level text from a PDF), each element is split into lines and flattened.
required


index
Iterable[int]
Explicit line numbers to associate with lines. If not provided, line numbers are assigned sequentially starting from zero.
None

title: NumberedLines
text:
Notes

NumberedLines is immutable: slicing and filtering return new objects rather than modifying the original.
The class does not perform any I/O. Display and printing are left to the caller.
The object can be passed directly to pd.Series() or other APIs that accept a sequence of strings.

title: NumberedLines
text:
Examples
Create from a single string:
>>> nl = NumberedLines("a\nb\nc")
>>> nl.index
[0, 1, 2]
Slice while preserving original line numbers:
>>> nl[1:3].index
[1, 2]
Reset indices after slicing:
>>> nl[1:3].reset_index().index
[0, 1]

title: era_pl: empirical research in accounting with Python
text:
era_pl provides Polars data and functions for the Python/Polars edition of Empirical Research in Accounting: Tools and Methods. Install the era-py distribution and import era_pl in Python. This is the API used by the book and its companion materials.
The same distribution also supplies the era_py pandas/Ibis API. Both namespaces use the same packaged datasets, but their function coverage and arguments differ.
See the changelog for recent additions and fixes, or the Python/Polars book for worked examples. The function reference describes the APIs, and the dataset catalog documents the included data.

title: era_pl: empirical research in accounting with Python
text:
Installation
Install the package with its Polars extra:
pip install "era-py[polars]"
Add the extras required for your workflow:
pip install "era-py[polars,tables]"
pip install "era-py[polars,plots]"
Python 3.10 or later is required. The Polars extra requires Polars 2 or later.
The development version can be installed from GitHub:
pip install "era-py[polars] @ git+https://github.com/iangow/era_py.git"

title: era_pl: empirical research in accounting with Python
text:
Packaged data
Load a dataset and inspect its documentation:
from era_pl import data_info, load_data

camp = load_data("camp_attendance")
camp_info = data_info("camp_attendance")
data_info(name) returns a dataset’s description, source, dimensions, schema, and variable definitions without loading its observations. Use data_catalog() to inspect every packaged dataset.

title: era_pl: empirical research in accounting with Python
text:
Polars helpers
Importing era_pl also registers the .era namespace on Polars expressions and dataframes. For example, form quantile groups with:
import polars as pl
import era_pl

data = pl.DataFrame({"value": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]})
data.with_columns(bucket=pl.col("value").era.ntile(3))
The reference groups functions for event dates, data retrieval, models, data cleaning, tables, plots, and SEC indexes.

title: era_pl: empirical research in accounting with Python
text:
Pandas and Ibis API
For pandas workflows, install era-py and import era_py. Its Ibis/Postgres event-return and WRDS helpers additionally require pip install "era-py[ibis]". These functions have a separate section in the reference.
The era_pl event helpers currently construct event dates and windows; era_pl.get_event_rets() and era_pl.copy_inline() are unimplemented. Use the documented Ibis API where cumulative event-return calculations are needed.

title: Changelog
text: Release notes cover version 0.0.32 onward. Dates are the dates of publication on PyPI. For earlier changes, see the commit history.

title: Changelog
text:
Version 0.0.35 (2026-10-15)

Data and metadata

Added data_info(name) and data_catalog() to both era_py and era_pl. These provide dataset descriptions, sources, dimensions, schemas, and variable definitions for all 27 packaged datasets without loading their observations.
Refreshed aaer_dates from the canonical farr data, retaining all 3,386 reconciled rows, historical entries, and source-backed corrections.
Synchronized five public-float date corrections in iliev_2010 with farr, including four fractional years. All 7,214 observations are retained.



Functions and dependencies

Made Ibis an optional dependency. Install era-py[ibis] for the Ibis/Postgres event-study and WRDS helpers; the base API no longer requires Ibis.
Corrected era_pl’s ntile() expression to preserve nulls, exclude them from bucket counts, and assign larger buckets first, matching R/SQL behavior.
Updated Polars AdaBoost and RUSBoost to retain a perfect learner with weight 1, handle unusable learners, and report an error when none can be fitted.
Added validation of boosting probability weights: weights must be finite, nonnegative, and have a positive finite total. Predictions continue to use normalized weighted vote shares.
Fixed daily and monthly Ibis cumulative event returns for complete losses (ret = -1) in stocks and market or size benchmarks. Missing-value handling is unchanged; returns below -1 remain errors.



Validation

Added regression tests for the data, metadata, optional dependencies, Polars helpers, boosting, and Ibis event returns. CI now installs the Ibis and DuckDB dependencies needed for the event-return tests.

title: Changelog
text:
Version 0.0.34 (2026-10-12)

Aligned camp_attendance, iliev_2010, and test_scores with the teaching data in the R package farr.
Updated dataset metadata and tests for both the pandas and Polars loaders.

title: Changelog
text:
Version 0.0.33 (2026-10-07)

Added support for Polars 2 and required polars>=2.0.0 in the Polars extra.
Updated date-expression handling in the Polars data helpers and added compatibility tests for data loading and expression methods.

title: Changelog
text:
Version 0.0.32 (2026-10-04)

Added explicit parsing of string dates when restoring packaged Polars data and constructing event dates.
Normalized date inputs used to filter Fama-French daily factors.

Fit a binary boosting model using at most size learner attempts.
A learner that correctly classifies the full training data replaces all earlier learners and receives voting weight 1. Unusable learners stop AdaBoost (rus=False); RUSBoost skips them and tries another sample. Raise ValueError if no usable learner is fitted. Single-class data retain the ConstantProbModel fallback.

title: AAER dates from SEC
text:
Details
The SEC index was refreshed through October 8, 2026. Exact duplicate rows are removed; distinct entries sharing an AAER number are retained. Source-backed corrections retain November 16, 1999 for AAER-1209 and restore AAER-1470 dated October 23, 2001. Historical entries missing from the current index are preserved, including three intentionally omitted numbers with missing dates. The malformed historical identifier AAER-x2218 is replaced by AAER-2218. Raw snapshots, historical supplements, and the correction table with release links are maintained in data-raw; see also the refresh investigation (https://github.com/iangow/farr/issues/27). Index dates have not all been checked against the underlying releases.
